content.text:
I submitted index 14 (Al 0.29, Sb 0.71) as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.0079%, the highest of the three I measured. That uses the full merit budget of 3; I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Al : Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 20 | 0.11 : 0.89 | 0.0002 |
| 14 | 0.29 : 0.71 | 0.0079 |
| 12 | 0.39 : 0.61 | 0.0024 |

- **Why I started at the Sb-rich end:** MEGNet band-gap predictions put the Al–Sb phases AlSbO₄ (3.65 eV, stable on the hull) and Al₅Sb₃O₁₆ (3.74 eV) above the 2.4 eV illumination, so they can't absorb it. Sb-rich oxides such as Sb₆O₁₃ (2.05 eV) and SbO₂ (1.67 eV) can.
- **What the measurements showed:** EQE rose about 40× from index 20 to index 14, then fell by about 3× at index 12. With only three points, that suggests a peak somewhere around Sb 0.7 but doesn't pin it down.
- **Main uncertainty:** the peak could sit between the points I measured, at about Sb 0.66 or 0.75 (indices 13 and 15), and I had no budget left to check them. Al₂Sb₂O₇ at the 50:50 composition has a predicted gap of 1.04 eV, but I didn't run its stability check, and index 12 falling off gives no reason to expect a better point near there.
- **Absolute level:** every EQE here is very low (below 0.01%), so this system is a weak photoanode overall.
